display_name: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (USA, Europe) (En,Fr,De,Es,It,Nl,Da)

slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only one slot observed across both available .sav samples; no slot-select/header-compare logic found in the traced functions. The entire 512-byte buffer is rewritten as 64 x 8-byte EEPROM blocks on every save.

checksums.name: dirty_clean_marker
checksums.formula_detail: Single-byte state flag, not a mathematical checksum: FUN_080177fc writes 0xFE ('dirty') to offset 0x1FA and immediately flushes block 63 to EEPROM alone, then overwrites RAM with 0xAE ('clean') before the full 64-block rewrite flushes block 63 again as its final iteration. Detects a torn/incomplete save on next boot if power is lost mid-rewrite.

checksums.name: candidate_checksum_or_sequence
checksums.formula_detail: FUN_080177fc stores the return value of FUN_0800d1dc(0x1fc, ramBase) at offset 0x1FE-0x1FF. The decompiled body of FUN_0800d1dc (a 1-argument decrement loop) is inconsistent with being called with 2 arguments and producing a return value, and Ghidra flags a symbol-overlap warning at that address, so the true algorithm could not be recovered. sum8/sum16/xor8/xor16 were tested in Python over byte ranges [0:0x1f8], [0:0x1fa], [0:0x1fb], [0:0x1fc], [0:0x1fd] of saves/cap-01-future-1.sav; none reproduced the stored value 0x0505. A table-driven CRC engine (FUN_0800d1a0) exists nearby but its 256-entry table is ROM data not present in this workspace, so CRC could not be tested either.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 block-transfer primitive: programs DMA3 source/destination/control registers (param_1=SAD, param_2=DAD, param_3|0x80000000=CNT with start bit) and busy-waits for completion, restoring the saved IRQ-mask snapshot on exit. Used by both the EEPROM read and write primitives to move bitstreams to/from the EEPROM backdoor address 0x0D000000.

EEPROM block READ primitive (blockIndex, destBuffer). Packs a 2-bit read opcode + 6-bit block address, clocks it out via FUN_0805b570, then reads 68 bits back via a second FUN_0805b570 transfer and unpacks the trailing 64 bits into 4x16-bit words at destBuffer.

EEPROM block WRITE primitive (blockIndex, srcData[4], waitFlag). Packs 8 bytes of data + 6-bit address + 2-bit write opcode and clocks the whole bitstream out in one FUN_0805b570 transfer, then busy-polls the EEPROM ready bit at 0x0D000000 with a bounded retry loop.
Thin wrapper: FUN_0805b6b4(blockIndex, buffer, waitFlag=1). This is the actual 'write block and wait' entry point called by the save flush routine.

Write-verify helper: reads back a just-written block via FUN_0805b5f0 into a local buffer and word-compares it against the expected data pointer supplied by the caller; returns 0x8000 on mismatch, else 0.

Boot-time scan: iterates all blocks via FUN_0805b5f0, checking for an out-of-range status to detect an unformatted/absent EEPROM save. No caller of this function was found in the available 97-function trace.

Save-flush controller. Sets dirty marker (0xFE) at offset 0x1FA, immediately flushes block 63 alone, flips marker to clean (0xAE) in RAM, computes and stores the candidate checksum/sequence field at 0x1FE-0x1FF, then writes+verifies all 64 blocks in order (block 63 last, carrying the finalized marker+checksum).

Candidate checksum/sequence function. Decompiled body (1-arg decrement loop) is inconsistent with its 2-argument call site and carries a Ghidra symbol-overlap warning; treat the recovered body as unreliable. Algorithm unverified against the one available non-blank sample.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Save entry wrapper: calls FUN_080177fc() and dispatches to a generic error handler (func_0x08002bc0, not in this extraction) on any non-zero return. The true in-game trigger (menu action, autosave checkpoint, etc.) that calls FUN_0802933c was not found in the available 97-function trace.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced statically in ghidra/decompiled.c: FUN_0802933c's only call is to FUN_080177fc; FUN_080177fc's calls to func_0x0805b6a0/func_0x0805b814 were cross-referenced against ghidra/save_related_functions.c's pre-extracted EEPROM seed functions and confirmed by matching the resulting byte deltas (0xFE/0xAE at offset 0x1FA) against saves/cap-01-future-1.sav.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Per-block write-verify: after each block write, FUN_080177fc calls FUN_0805b814 to read the block back and compare it against the data that was supposed to have been written.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced statically: FUN_0805b814's body calls FUN_0805b5f0 (the read primitive) then compares against its second argument, matching the call pattern in FUN_080177fc's main loop.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot-time save-presence/validity scan, reading all blocks sequentially. No caller found in this extraction; inferred to run at game boot/title-screen based on its role and lack of any write operations.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced statically by following FUN_08017788's calls to func_0x0805b5f0 in ghidra/decompiled.c; no dynamic/runtime trace evidence available to confirm when it executes.

fields.name: unmapped_payload_region
fields.update_mechanism: Rewritten in full as part of every save (blocks 0-62 of the 64-block loop in FUN_080177fc), but no individual sub-field was exercised in either available sample (both are new/near-empty saves), so no internal layout could be mapped.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c FUN_080177fc main loop; both saves/*.sav show this entire range at the 0xFF fill value

fields.name: unattributed_tail_bytes_1f8_1f9
fields.update_mechanism: Not written by any function in the traced save-flush chain; must be populated by gameplay code outside this extraction before FUN_080177fc runs and is simply carried along as part of block 63's 8 bytes during the write/verify cycle.
fields.evidence: No match found in ghidra/decompiled.c for a writer targeting this offset; byte change observed only via saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt diff between the two samples

fields.name: dirty_clean_marker
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_080177fc writes 0xFE then flushes block 63 alone, then writes 0xAE in RAM before the 64-block loop re-flushes block 63 last. Crash-safety marker, not a magic signature.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c FUN_080177fc; observed terminal byte 0xae at offset 0x1fa in saves/cap-01-future-1.sav matches the traced 'clean' write

fields.name: unattributed_byte_1fb
fields.update_mechanism: Always fill value in both available samples; not written by any traced function.
fields.evidence: saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt shows no change at this offset between samples

fields.name: unattributed_byte_1fd
fields.update_mechanism: Changes between samples but has no attributable writer in the traced save-flush chain; possibly related to the same unresolved-origin field as offset 0x1F8-0x1F9.

fields.name: candidate_checksum_or_sequence
fields.update_mechanism: FUN_080177fc stores the return of FUN_0800d1dc(0x1fc, ramBase) here. Call-site arguments suggest a value derived from bytes 0x000-0x1FB, but the decompiled body of FUN_0800d1dc does not match its call signature (Ghidra symbol-overlap warning), so the exact formula is unverified. sum8/sum16/xor8/xor16 over multiple candidate ranges were tested against the stored value 0x0505 and none matched.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c FUN_080177fc and FUN_0800d1dc; Python verification in SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 4 against saves/cap-01-future-1.sav

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip the dirty/clean marker from 0xAE back to 0xFE on an otherwise-clean save, then reload
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If any unrecovered loader branches on this byte, the save should be treated as incomplete/corrupt on next boot; if not, no observable effect.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero both bytes of the candidate checksum/sequence field (0x0505 -> 0x0000) while leaving the marker and payload intact
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Falsifies or confirms the 'write-only, never load-validated' hypothesis from section 4: if the save loads identically, the field is not checked on load within the traced boot-scan path; if the save is rejected/reset, a load-time validator exists outside this extraction.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip a single byte in the always-0xFF payload region (e.g. offset 0x000) from 0xFF to 0x00 on a fresh save, then reload
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: First evidence of what (if anything) occupies this region; either an observable gameplay/UI change, or the byte gets silently overwritten back to 0xFF by normal save logic.

open_questions: Exact algorithm for the 2-byte field at offset 0x1FE-0x1FF (candidate checksum/sequence) — FUN_0800d1dc's recovered body is inconsistent with its call signature and could not be independently verified against the single available non-blank sample.
Origin/writer of the bytes at offset 0x1F8-0x1F9 and 0x1FD, which change between samples but are not written by any function reachable from the traced save-flush chain in this workspace.

Whether a load-time validator checks the marker byte (0x1FA) or the candidate checksum field (0x1FE-0x1FF) before accepting a save — FUN_08017788 (the only traced boot-scan function) does not reference either offset specifically in the extracted code.
The actual in-game trigger that calls FUN_0802933c (menu save action, autosave checkpoint, etc.) — its caller was not present in the 97-function trace-guided extraction.

Whether a second/backup slot exists elsewhere in the 512-byte buffer — not observed in either available sample, but only 2 of the 6 referenced .sav snapshots in the corpus metadata were present in this workspace, limiting sample coverage.
Purpose of the 512-byte memcpy-style copy (func_0x0805d3c0) performed after a fully successful save in FUN_080177fc — its destination buffer's role (shadow copy, UI cache, etc.) is unresolved.
Exact RAM segment (EWRAM 0x02xxxxxx vs IWRAM 0x03xxxxxx) backing the symbolic _DAT_0801786c save mirror base pointer — not resolvable from symbolic Ghidra globals alone.
